From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-01T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer & DPF questionnaire — initial submission

Samantha,

Thanks — received the spreadsheet. I've done an initial pass and attached a draft answers pack (DPF-answers-draft.pdf) and a simplified dataflow diagram (dataflow-diagram.png) that maps our processing stages to the clauses in the DPA Annex. High-level notes:

- Cross-border basis: Redwood uses standard contractual clauses (SCCs) for EU->US transfers; we publish a DPF mapping showing supplemental technical and organisational measures.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a live roster; critical infra subs (cloud providers, telemetry) are emailed to customers 30 days before onboarding. For regulated accounts we can agree to a longer notice.
- Retention: application-layer retention is customer-configurable; for hosted accounts default is 90 days for short-term KV/cache, 365 days for logs, with options for longer retention on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Audit logs: token-level request logs and per-request traces are available; standard retention is 365 days (extendable).

Attachments: DPF-answers-draft.pdf (pdf, 98KB); dataflow-diagram.png (png, 420KB)

Propose a call Wednesday 11:00 BST / 03:00 PT (I can also do 15:00 BST). If you can share three times that work for your privacy team, I'll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Andre Muller <andre.muller@clearmeds.eu>

Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearwellhealth.com>, procurement@clearwellhealth.com
Date: 2027-07-05T14:22:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Data transfer & DPF questionnaire — initial submission

Hannah — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying items after reviewing the draft PDF:

1) SCCs and DPF: your note references an internal "DPF mapping". Could you surface the exact mapping table showing which SCC clause maps to which technical measure (encryption in transit/rest, key custody, personnel access controls)? Our privacy team needs a one-page clause->control table.

2) Subprocessor notifications: the 30-day notice for critical infra is good. For any subprocessor with access to content (model training or telemetry), would Redwood consent to a contractual clause that requires explicit customer approval for use on regulated PHI workloads? We may need that for parts of our product.

3) Retention variants: can Redwood provide an example config snippet (or refer to the Console setting) that shows how a customer would change token-level retention from 90 days to 30/180/365? A screenshot or a short step list would be helpful.

4) Audit evidence: for SOC2-like evidence, do you produce a sample audit log extract or schema? If so, can you share an anonymized sample (CSV) and the fields that we can expect (timestamp, request_id, model_id, token_count, requester_id, region, region_routing)?

Please see inline from your PDF where we added a few in-line comments — I can forward the annotated copy if that helps. We'd also like to review an SCC execution plan template you use for customers.

Thanks,
Andre Muller
Privacy & Compliance
ClearMed Solutions (EU)
